rationale: Both candidates clearly hit only one solid ground-truth thread (the --task-type choices/validation regression, GT's P2 item), missing GT's core P1s about combined-mode Cache-DiT coverage, the modular-alias metadata contract, and Ref2VA's implicit task default, as well as all four SamitHuang code-quality nits. Y shows deeper, more concretely verified investigation in the same subsystem areas (cache-dit dotted-module handling, supported_tasks/Ref2VA edge cases, exception-guard removal) with actual reproductions (tracebacks, '104 passed' test run) and a clearer prioritized Blocking/Should-fix/Worth-considering structure plus a real CI-red catch, giving it a modest edge in recall, precision, and actionability. X is also well-evidenced and systematic but its extra findings (torch.compile default scope, weight-loader contiguity gaps) sit further from the ground-truth concerns and lack the same verification depth.
